answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a decaying work-bond: each identity posts stake that only becomes transferable after it publishes a unique artifact and waits through a review horizon of two full epochs. Peer graders then set an identity anchor—a merklized hash of that artifact, a hardware-attested nonce, and the spend key—so clones cannot cheaply fork the record. Until the bond clears, new agents may only harbor inbound transfers in escrow and cannot vote, grade, or issue invites. A proven duplicate slashes the bond to the graders, making mass farming slow and expensive.
